title: Cerevance Parkinson’s drug shortens 'off time' in Ph. 3, paving path to FDA
snippet: The Takeda spinout showed that a high dose of solengepras can shorten the periods during which difficult Parkinson’s disease symptoms like involuntary movements and sleepiness.

title: ArriVent sheds nearly half of value on late-stage lung cancer miss
snippet: ArriVent BioPharma’s Phase 3 lung cancer trial was clouded by stronger-than-expected data for patients receiving chemotherapy, prompting analysts to pivot focus to a late-stage test of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor in a different type of lung cancer and to the biotech’s antibody-drug conjugate pipeline.

title: Biotech VC Forbion raises record $2.6B to support 30 ‘high-potential’ companies
snippet: Forbion participated in the November 2025 series B round of Gate Bioscience, which earlier this week inked an up to $870 million deal extension with Eli Lilly.

title: Doudna’s CAR T biotech Caribou to end R&D activities, slash staff as financing freezes up
snippet: Caribou Biosciences entered the scene in 2011 and went public in 2021. Over the course of its existence, the biotech has received funding and support from a handful of Big Pharma players, including Novartis, AbbVie and Pfizer.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Bayer commits $2.2B to build pharma manufacturing plant in Ohio
snippet: The investment will equip Bayer to make oncology, cardiovascular and renal care ingredients and drugs.

title: Genmab and AbbVie’s Epkinly win, a rush of deals, Sarepta’s turnaround hopes, more
snippet: New data for Genmab and AbbVie’s bispecific antibody Epkinly wowed analysts and could set the partners up for an expanded approval in diffuse large B cell lymphoma; deals have flowed steadily this week, including Novartis’ nearly $8 billion bet on mRNA drugs with China’s Abogen Biosciences; and could Sarepta Therapeut...

title: Why executive candidates need the truth, not the sales pitch
snippet: The person you expect to address the company’s problems should know the challenges your business faces. Not having that context will limit what they can accomplish.

title: 5 biggest venture capital raises of Q3 2026
snippet: Venture capital continued to flow into biopharma in the third quarter, though experts pointed out that investors remained selective, preferring to put their money behind advanced and derisked assets, as well as AI-driven drugmakers.

title: Adecto, Aviceda shut down
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Shionogi makes $2B rare disease play with IntraBio buy
snippet: With its acquisition of IntraBio, Shionogi will gain ownership over Aqneursa, which could hit peak global sales of $1 billion across its two indications in Niemann-Pick disease type C and ataxia-telangiectasia, according to Jefferies.

title: FDA extends review of Novo’s hemophilia A drug, citing manufacturing issues
snippet: Despite the regulatory delay, Novo is still expecting a 2027 launch for its hemophilia A drug denecimig.

title: AbbVie, Genmab's Epkinly sets ‘new standard of care’ in first-line lymphoma in Phase 3
snippet: AbbVie and Genmab’s bispecific antibody blew analyst expectations out of the water with a 51% improvement in progression-free survival when used alongside a standard frontline regimen in diffuse large B cell lymphoma—potentially setting up a battle with Roche's Polivy.

title: Compliance concerns hinder rollout of AI in drug manufacturing: Survey
snippet: While AI is taking off in biopharma for administrative tasks and drug discovery efforts, more than 90% of drugmakers have yet to commit to scaling AI use in regulated biopharma manufacturing, according to CRB’s new Horizons: Life Sciences report.

title: BioSpace 40 Under 40 winners make their mark on biopharma
snippet: 40 Under 40 honorees’ accomplishments include co-developing the world’s first synthetic biology programming language for mRNA and co-founding and leading a company acquired for $700 million up-front and up to $1.225 billion in total consideration.

title: Significant stock movers of September: Viking soars, Longeveron slides
snippet: Viking Therapeutics rode strong obesity data before a major capital raise, while Longeveron’s mid-stage setback prompted questions about its future.

title: 2 Massachusetts biotechs call it quits
snippet: Adecto Pharmaceuticals has ceased operations, while Aviceda Therapeutics is in the process of winding down.

title: Lilly doubles down on Gate alliance to unlock new drug class with another $870M+ in biobucks
snippet: Eli Lilly first linked up with Gate Bioscience in July 2025 to leverage the biotech’s “Molecular Gate” engine to treat diseases with high unmet need. Monday’s expansion will add one undisclosed target to the existing agreement, with an option for a second.

title: Genentech pens $1.27B deal to access Alector’s preclinical blood-brain barrier asset
snippet: After a series of clinical-stage failures, Alector is resetting around its preclinical blood-brain barrier delivery technology, securing a big pharma partnership along the way.

title: CSL strikes up to $1.6B deal with Alentis for autoimmune drug with broad potential
snippet: CSL will co-develop and co-promote Alentis Therapeutics' anti-claudin-1 therapy lixudebart for kidney and liver conditions, including primary sclerosing cholangitis and a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by small blood vessel inflammation.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
